part.text: I’m comparing equal-length clock windows (night: 6 p.m.–6 a.m.; day: 6 a.m.–6 p.m.) using crash counts and crash outcomes. The file has no traffic-volume or pedestrian/cyclist exposure denominator, so it can show reported crash burden and severity conditional on a crash, but not danger per trip or per road user.

+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import duckdb
+import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
+import pandas as pd
+
+
+OUT = Path("out")
+con = duckdb.connect()
+summary = con.execute(
+    """
+    WITH crashes AS (
+      SELECT
+        CASE WHEN EXTRACT(HOUR FROM crash_time) >= 18
+                  OR EXTRACT(HOUR FROM crash_time) < 6
+             THEN 'Night (6pm–6am)' ELSE 'Day (6am–6pm)' END AS period,
+        COALESCE(number_of_persons_injured, 0) AS injured,
+        COALESCE(number_of_persons_killed, 0) AS killed
+      FROM read_parquet('data/crashes.parquet')
+    )
+    SELECT period,
+           COUNT(*) AS crashes,
+           COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE injured > 0 OR killed > 0) AS injury_or_fatal_crashes,
+           COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE killed > 0) AS fatal_crashes
+    FROM crashes
+    GROUP BY period
+    """
+).df()
+
+order = ["Day (6am–6pm)", "Night (6pm–6am)"]
+summary["period"] = pd.Categorical(summary["period"], categories=order, ordered=True)
+summary = summary.sort_values("period").reset_index(drop=True)
+summary["injury_or_fatal_pct"] = summary.injury_or_fatal_crashes / summary.crashes * 100
+summary["fatal_crash_pct"] = summary.fatal_crashes / summary.crashes * 100
+summary["fatal_crashes_per_1000"] = summary.fatal_crashes / summary.crashes * 1000
+
+
+def bar_chart(values, labels, title, ylabel, path, value_format, color):
+    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8.2, 5.1))
+    bars = ax.bar(labels, values, color=color, width=0.62)
+    ax.set_title(title, loc="left", fontsize=15, weight="bold", pad=15)
+    ax.set_ylabel(ylabel)
+    ax.spines[["top", "right"]].set_visible(False)
+    ax.grid(axis="y", alpha=0.23)
+    ax.set_axisbelow(True)
+    upper = max(values) * 1.2 if max(values) else 1
+    ax.set_ylim(0, upper)
+    for bar, val in zip(bars, values):
+        ax.text(bar.get_x() + bar.get_width() / 2, bar.get_height() + upper * 0.025,
+                value_format(val), ha="center", va="bottom", fontsize=11, weight="bold")
+    fig.text(0.01, 0.01,
+             "NYC police-reported crashes; night = 6pm–6am, day = 6am–6pm. "
+             "Crash records do not measure traffic exposure.", fontsize=9, color="#444444")
+    fig.tight_layout(rect=(0, 0.07, 1, 1))
+    fig.savefig(path, dpi=180, bbox_inches="tight")
+    plt.close(fig)
+
+
+display = summary.copy()
+display["period"] = display["period"].astype(str)
+
+# Option 1: crash burden by equal-length time-of-day window.
+v1 = display[["period", "crashes"]].copy()
+v1.to_csv(OUT / "values_1.csv", index=False)
+bar_chart(v1.crashes.tolist(), ["Day\n6am–6pm", "Night\n6pm–6am"],
+          "More crashes are recorded during daytime hours", "Police-reported crashes",
+          OUT / "option_1.png", lambda x: f"{x:,.0f}", ["#557A95", "#263F5B"])
+
+# Option 2: chance of any reported injury or death, conditional on a crash.
+v2 = display[["period", "crashes", "injury_or_fatal_crashes", "injury_or_fatal_pct"]].copy()
+v2["injury_or_fatal_pct"] = v2["injury_or_fatal_pct"].round(4)
+v2.to_csv(OUT / "values_2.csv", index=False)
+bar_chart(display.injury_or_fatal_pct.tolist(), ["Day\n6am–6pm", "Night\n6pm–6am"],
+          "A larger share of nighttime crashes involve injury or death", "Crashes with ≥1 injured or killed person (%)",
+          OUT / "option_2.png", lambda x: f"{x:.1f}%", ["#557A95", "#263F5B"])
+
+# Option 3: crash-level fatality rate, conditional on a crash.
+v3 = display[["period", "crashes", "fatal_crashes", "fatal_crash_pct", "fatal_crashes_per_1000"]].copy()
+v3["fatal_crash_pct"] = v3["fatal_crash_pct"].round(5)
+v3["fatal_crashes_per_1000"] = v3["fatal_crashes_per_1000"].round(4)
+v3.to_csv(OUT / "values_3.csv", index=False)
+bar_chart(display.fatal_crashes_per_1000.tolist(), ["Day\n6am–6pm", "Night\n6pm–6am"],
+          "Fatal crashes are more frequent per crash at night", "Fatal crashes per 1,000 crashes",
+          OUT / "option_3.png", lambda x: f"{x:.2f}", ["#557A95", "#263F5B"])
+
+day, night = display.iloc[0], display.iloc[1]
+options = {
+    "options": [
+        {
+            "id": 1,
+            "metric": "Police-reported crash count",
+            "denominator": "Equal-length 12-hour day or night window over the dataset period; total counts, not exposure-adjusted rates",
+            "grouping": "Day (6am–6pm) vs night (6pm–6am)",
+            "chart_type": "bar chart",
+            "reason": "Crash counts show the absolute reported crash burden in the two equal-length daily time windows.",
+            "probability": 0.35,
+            "answer": f"NYC recorded {int(night.crashes):,} crashes at night versus {int(day.crashes):,} during the day, about {(1-night.crashes/day.crashes)*100:.1f}% fewer nighttime crashes.",
+            "interpretation": "This framing answers when more police-reported crashes occurred and shows greater daytime crash volume. Equal 12-hour windows make the clock-time comparison straightforward, but crash counts alone do not show risk per trip or per road user; the dataset lacks traffic exposure data."
+        },
+        {
+            "id": 2,
+            "metric": "Share of crashes with at least one person injured or killed",
+            "denominator": "All police-reported crashes in each period",
+            "grouping": "Day (6am–6pm) vs night (6pm–6am)",
+            "chart_type": "bar chart",
+            "reason": "The crash-level injury-or-fatality share measures how often a reported crash resulted in human harm, regardless of crash volume.",
+            "probability": 0.40,
+            "answer": f"{night.injury_or_fatal_pct:.1f}% of nighttime crashes involved an injury or death, compared with {day.injury_or_fatal_pct:.1f}% of daytime crashes, a difference of {night.injury_or_fatal_pct-day.injury_or_fatal_pct:.1f} percentage points.",
+            "interpretation": "This framing answers whether a crash was more likely to involve reported human harm at night and shows a higher share for nighttime crashes. It is a defensible crash-severity comparison because each crash is the denominator, but it does not account for how many people or vehicles were on the road, nor establish risk per trip."
+        },
+        {
+            "id": 3,
+            "metric": "Fatal-crash rate per 1,000 police-reported crashes",
+            "denominator": "All police-reported crashes in each period",
+            "grouping": "Day (6am–6pm) vs night (6pm–6am)",
+            "chart_type": "bar chart",
+            "reason": "A crash-level fatality rate isolates the most severe recorded outcome and avoids confusing the higher daytime crash count with fatality severity.",
+            "probability": 0.25,
+            "answer": f"There were {night.fatal_crashes_per_1000:.2f} fatal crashes per 1,000 nighttime crashes versus {day.fatal_crashes_per_1000:.2f} per 1,000 daytime crashes (about {(night.fatal_crashes_per_1000/day.fatal_crashes_per_1000):.1f} times as high at night).",
+            "interpretation": "This framing answers whether a reported crash was more likely to be fatal at night and shows a higher nighttime fatal-crash rate. It is a defensible measure of crash-level fatal severity, but does not estimate an individual road user's risk because traffic volume and road-user exposure are absent."
+        }
+    ]
+}
+(OUT / "options.json").write_text(json.dumps(options, indent=2) + "\n")
+
+print(display.to_string(index=False))
*** End Patch
